subject: Request: Interim control affirmation for SOC 2 post-report window
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@tiltworks.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@tiltworks.ai
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for interim control affirmation to cover post-report period

Hi Priyom,

Hope you’re well. TiltWorks completed Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II coverage review in December 2025 and we're proceeding with our vendor-risk sign-off. Our security team has one outstanding ask: a short bridge/interim affirmation that covers the period after the report (2025-12-31) up to the present date, addressing any material changes that would affect the report scope. Specifically they’ve requested:

- Confirmation of no material control changes since 2025-12-31 (or a summary of changes)
- Any incidents or security exceptions since the report end date
- Confirmation of the continued applicability of the controls in the report (KMS, access controls, change management)
- A point of contact for any follow-up evidence requests

I've attached a short SOC2 Request Checklist that lists their preferred fields and timeline. Can Redwood provide a short bridge letter or interim control affirmation by end of week (5/7)? Brightwater (our auditor) is copied for context — they may want to see the draft.

Thank you — we appreciate quick confirmation so we can close this on our side.

Best,
Elena Morales
Sr. Vendor Risk Manager
TiltWorks

Elena — thanks for the note and the checklist. We can provide an interim affirmation/bridge letter that addresses the items you listed.

Plan:
- I’ll coordinate with Security (Karthik) for a short factual statement and exception log.
- Soojin (legal) will review language for audit-safe phrasing.
- Target: share a draft by Monday 5/4 so you and Brightwater have time to review ahead of your cutoff.

1) Is TiltWorks expecting a fully signed bridge letter (company exec signature) or is an auditor-reviewed affirmation sufficient?
2) Do you need control-level evidence (e.g., snapshot of IAM roles, KMS key policy) attached, or can we provide an index and make evidence available on request?

If you prefer a call to walk through the items, I’m available today between 3–5pm PT.

Thanks — looping in Soojin and Karthik.

— Priyom Das

On Fri, May 1, 2026 at 10:04 AM Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com> wrote:
> A few quick clarifying Qs to make the draft useful for your vendor team:
> 1) Is TiltWorks expecting a fully signed bridge letter (company exec signature) or is an auditor-reviewed affirmation sufficient?

Hi all — quick security check-in. We reviewed our control posture since 2025-12-31 and can confirm the following for the requested interim period through 2026-05-03:

- No production-impacting security incidents affecting the SOC 2 scope. There was one low-severity configuration issue in an internal staging cluster (2026-02-14) that was triaged and remediated within 24 hours; it did not involve customer data or production systems.
- No changes to our KMS root or customer-data encryption policies; we rotated a subset of CMK keys as part of scheduled key rotation (routine, documented).
- Access control changes since the report: normal hires and role updates were applied using our documented access provisioning flow; no emergency access exceptions were created.
- Change management: we continued to run the same approved change control process; there were no retrospective exceptions.

I’m attaching a draft redwood_bridge_draft_v1.pdf that frames these facts in bridge-letter language; legal has reviewed a baseline. Priyom / Soojin — happy to adjust wording if TiltWorks/Brightwater prefer more auditor-specific phrasing.

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Security (acting)
Redwood Inference

- Attached evidence-index.xlsx lists artifacts we can share on request (IAM snapshots, KMS key rotation logs, incident ticket reference). For any artifact you want full copies of, send the list and we’ll provide secure links.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.
